title: Memory Management in Closures
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of memory management in closures in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply capture lists in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on memory management in closures and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Capture lists”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Reusable functions and precise data models reduce duplication. Handling missing data and failures explicitly makes later application code safer to change.

content_blocks.title: Reference Lifetime and ARC
content_blocks.alt_text: The diagram shows how two strong references can form a cycle and why a weak reference can break the cycle when the lifetime model permits it.
content_blocks.caption: Strong reference cycles can keep class instances alive.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** A closure packages behavior that can be passed or stored. Check which values it captures and whether it can outlive the current call before choosing capture semantics.

**Work through the lesson.** Reason about copies, identity, ARC, object lifetime, and the boundary between safe and unsafe memory access. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.text: Asynchronous execution can suspend while work waits; it is not automatically the same as parallel execution. Design cancellation, error propagation, task lifetime, and shared-state isolation deliberately.
